source.title: On an Open Question in Recovering Sturm--Liouville-Type Operators with Delay

accepted.question_text: Consider the delayed Sturm-Liouville inverse spectral problem in which, for j=0,1, L_j(a,q) is defined by -y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=lambda y(x) on 0<x<pi with boundary conditions y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0, where q is a complex-valued L2(0,pi) potential satisfying q(x)=0 on (0,a), and a is in (0,pi). Given the two spectra {lambda_{n,0}} and {lambda_{n,1}}, for which ranges of the delay parameter a and for which admissible boundary-condition types does this data uniquely determine q, and for which choices does uniqueness fail?
accepted.context_brief: Classification of uniqueness ranges and boundary conditions

evidence.quote: For $j=0,1,$ denote by $\{\lambda_{n,j}\}$ the spectrum of the boundary value problem ${\cal L}_j(a,q)$ of the form $-y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=\lambda y(x),\quad 0<x<\pi,$ $y(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0,$ where $q(x)$ is a complex-valued function in $L_2(0,\pi)$ and $q(x)=0$ on $(0,a),$ while $a\in(0,\pi).$
{\bf Inverse Problem 1.} Given the spectra $\{\lambda_{n,0}\}$ and $\{\lambda_{n,1}\},$ find the potential $q(x).$

Theorem~1 opens the analogous type of questions for Inverse Problem~1, which consist in giving description of ranges of the delay parameter $a$ along with the types of boundary conditions, for which the uniqueness of solution of Inverse Problem~1 takes place.

accepted.question_text: For each degenerate regime of the delayed Sturm-Liouville two-spectra inverse problem in which uniqueness fails, describe the corresponding classes of iso-bispectral potentials: distinct complex-valued L2(0,pi) potentials q satisfying q(x)=0 on (0,a) such that the boundary value problems L_0(a,q) and L_1(a,q) have one and the same pair of spectra.

evidence.quote: Namely, for each such $a,$ we construct an infinite family of different iso-bispectral potentials~$q(x),$ i.e. of those for which the problems ${\cal L}_0(a,q)$ and ${\cal L}_1(a,q)$ have one and the same pair of spectra.
In the opposite degenerate cases, it would be interesting to describe classes of iso-bispectral potentials.

accepted.question_text: Determine the uniqueness or nonuniqueness behavior of the delayed Sturm-Liouville two-spectra inverse problem for arbitrarily small positive delays a, where -y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=lambda y(x) is close to the classical a=0 Sturm-Liouville equation -y''(x)+q(x)y(x)=lambda y(x). For small a>0, does the pair of spectra {lambda_{n,0}} and {lambda_{n,1}} recover q uniquely, and if not, what iso-bispectral families occur?

evidence.quote: One of the first results in the inverse spectral theory says that the spectra of two boundary value problems for one and the same Sturm--Liouville equation with one common boundary condition: $-y''(x)+q(x)y(x)=\lambda y(x), \quad y(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0, \quad j=0,1,$ uniquely determine the potential $q(x).$
It is especially important to investigate the case of arbitrarily small values of $a$ making the problem ''close'' to the classical case~(\ref{0}).

accepted.question_text: For Robin-type variants of the delayed Sturm-Liouville inverse spectral problem, where the boundary conditions y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0 are replaced by y'(0)-h y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0 with complex h, determine whether an iso-bispectral counterexample analogous to the one constructed for y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0 can be built, or whether the two spectra continue to determine the potential q uniquely in the corresponding delay ranges.

evidence.quote: Instead of (\ref{2}), one could alternatively impose the boundary conditions $y'(0)-hy(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0$ with a complex parameter $h,$ which can be found given the input data of Inverse Problem~1.
Some discussion on a possibility of constructing a similar counterexample for other types of boundary conditions is provided, and new open questions are outlined.

However, the main difference from the case of boundary conditions (\ref{2}) is that, in the case of (\ref{rob}), there is no relation analogous to (\ref{3.6.1}). In other words, the constant $\omega$ is not determined by the function $w_1(x).$ Thus, each characteristic function (\ref{3.3}) and (\ref{3.4}) could depend on $\alpha$ even if $w_1(x)$ did not. So the presented scheme does not refute the uniqueness theorem in~\cite{Yur20}.

Extracted the historical uniqueness question for a<pi/2, the paper's partial positive and negative answers, and the abstract's note about similar counterexamples for other boundary conditions.

Extracted three current prospects from Remark 1: classify delay ranges and boundary-condition types for uniqueness, describe iso-bispectral potentials in degenerate cases, and investigate arbitrarily small delays.
Extracted the Robin-boundary-condition issue: the constructed scheme fails in its present form because omega is not determined by w_1, so it does not refute the cited uniqueness theorem.
Expanded the classification question with the definition of L_j(a,q), the admissible potential class, and the two-spectra input data from Inverse Problem 1.
Expanded the iso-bispectral-potential question using the paper's definition of iso-bispectrality and Remark 1's degenerate-case prompt.
Expanded the arbitrarily-small-delay question by stating the delayed equation and the classical a=0 comparison explicitly.
Expanded the other-boundary-conditions question for the Robin-type boundary conditions explicitly introduced in the paper and tied it to the failed counterexample strategy in Remark 2.
